MOTIVUS .
PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS
Team Member Competency Self-Assessment
Competencies and Industry Experience - the two screens where a team member says what they know and which industries they have worked in.
01 Overview
A team member signs in and lands on a home screen that shows their name and email and offers four tiles. Two of those tiles are covered here.
Competencies shows the company's full list of skills as one big table. For each skill the member can tick a level: Learner, Practitioner, or Expert. The list holds several hundred skills, so the screen is built around filtering. The member narrows the table down to the few rows that apply to them, ticks a level, and moves on.
Industry Experience does the same thing for industries instead of skills: which sectors the member has worked in.
A member only ever edits their own record. There is no way to pick another person, and there is no approval step - ticking a box saves it.
02 Scope
IN SCOPE
· Competencies - browse, filter, and rate skills
· Industry Experience - record industries worked in
· What both screens share: the home screen, the header with the home and info buttons, and the small-screen block
OUT OF SCOPE
· About Me
· Endorsements
· Adding or editing the skill and industry lists themselves
· Anything that reads this data later, such as search or reports
03 Competencies
One table: the skill list on the left, three tick boxes on the right, and a filter row above them.

Competencies, no filters applied. The header has a home button, the screen title, and an info button. The filter row has the Type and Area dropdowns, a search box for the skill name, and the Mine and New switches. Every row has Learner, Practitioner, and Expert tick boxes.
How skills are organised
Every skill sits in three levels: a Type, an Area inside that Type, and the skill itself inside that Area. Types include Agility, Backend, and Data Analytics. Areas include Agile and DevOps Coaching, API Paradigms & Communication Protocols, and Search & Indexing Platforms. Skill names are written as Vendor / Product when one vendor makes several tools - Atlassian / Jira, Azure DevOps / Pipelines - and as just the product name otherwise - GraphQL, Elasticsearch, SOAP. :selected:

Filtered, with two skills rated. Picking Type Backend and Area API Paradigms & Communication Protocols cuts the table down to four rows. GraphQL is set to Learner. REST is set to Practitioner, and its Learner box is ticked and greyed out - the app ticked it automatically and the member cannot untick it on its own.
Requirements
FR-C-01
Show all skills in a table.
Columns, left to right: Type, Area, Competency, Learner, Practitioner, Expert. The table opens with no filters, sorted by Type, then Area, then skill name.
FR-C-02
Filter by Type.
A dropdown lists every Type. Picking one shows only that Type's rows. It starts empty, which means no filter.
FR-C-03
Filter by Area, based on the Type picked.
The Area dropdown only lists Areas that belong to the Type currently picked, so the member can never choose a pair that returns no rows.
FR-C-04
Search by skill name.
A text box matches on the skill name. It works together with the Type and Area filters, not instead of them.
FR-C-05
"Mine" switch - show only skills the member has rated.
Off by default. When on, the table shows only rows where the member has ticked at least one level, so they can review their own profile without scrolling the whole list.
FR-C-06
"New" switch - show only recently added skills.
Off by default. When on, the table shows only skills added since the member last used the screen, so they can rate what is new without reading everything again. :selected:
FR-C-07
Filters work together.
Type, Area, the search box, Mine, and New all apply at the same time. The table updates as soon as any of them changes - there is no Apply button.
FR-C-08
Rate a skill at one of three levels.
Each row has a Learner, a Practitioner, and an Expert tick box. Rated and unrated skills appear in the same table, so the member can see what they have not filled in yet.
FR-C-09
Higher levels tick the lower ones automatically.
Ticking a level also ticks every level below it. Those boxes are shown greyed out and cannot be unticked on their own - a member can never be a Practitioner without also being a Learner. Unticking the level the member chose clears the ones it filled in.
FR-C-10
Save as soon as a box is ticked. There is no Save button. Ticking or unticking a box saves straight away, and unticking removes the rating completely.
FR-C-11
A member only sees their own ratings. The table has no column for who rated what, and there is no way to look at or change someone else's ratings.
FR-C-12
Explain the three levels. The info button in the header opens a short description of what Learner, Practitioner, and Expert mean, so everyone rates themselves the same way.
FR-C-13
Go back to the home screen. The home button in the header returns to the four tiles. Ratings already saved stay saved.
04 Industry Experience
The same idea as Competencies, but for industries: a list the company maintains, and the member ticks the ones they have worked in.
FR-I-01
Open from the home screen. The "Industry Experience" tile is third on the home screen, between Competencies and Endorsements.
FR-I-02
Show the list of industries. Industries come from a list the company maintains. The member picks from it and cannot type in their own, so the values stay the same for everyone.
FR-I-03
Tick each industry the member has worked in. Ticked and unticked industries appear in the same list.
FR-I-04
Save on tick, and show only the member's own record. Same as Competencies: no Save button, saves straight away, and a member only sees their own answers.
FR-I-05
Go back to the home screen. A home button in the header, the same as on Competencies.
05 Data model
The tables behind the two screens and how they connect.

IndustryExperience one row per member and industry
Notes
Store one level per skill, not three tick boxes. Because a higher level always fills in the lower ones, a single row holding the highest level the member picked says everything. The screen works out which lower boxes to grey out. Storing three separate true/false fields would let bad combinations exist in the database, such as Expert without Learner.
Type and Area are separate tables, not text fields. They are picked from dropdowns, and the Area dropdown depends on the Type. Keeping them as their own tables is what makes that possible.
Email identifies the member. It comes from the signed-in user and is what links their ratings and industries back to them.
06 General requirements
Things that apply to both screens.
FR-G-01
Show who is signed in. The home screen shows the member's name and email, taken from the sign-in. There is no way to switch to another user.
FR-G-02
Show four tiles on the home screen. About Me, Competencies, Industry Experience, and Endorsements, each an icon with a label underneath.
FR-G-03
Block screens that are too narrow. If the window is narrower than the supported width, the app hides its content and shows: "Sorry, this app is not formatted for mobile devices. Please use a desktop or tablet to do your self-assessment." This is based on window width, so a small desktop window triggers it too.
FR-G-04
Filtering must stay fast. Filtering is how the member gets through several hundred rows, so the table has to redraw quickly every time a filter changes.
FR-G-05
Record who saved what and when. Because one click saves straight away, every rating stores the member and the date it was saved. Unticking removes the rating and anything it filled in automatically.
MOTIVUS .
Team Member Competency Self-Assessment · PRD v0.3 . Competencies & Industry Experience :unselected:
